This vignette walks through a complete grading run end to end: writing tests,
gathering submissions, grading, summarising, and exporting.

## Folder layout

The grader expects one sub-folder per student under a submissions root, and a
flat folder of test files. File names follow a simple convention:

```
submissions/
  garcia_juan/
    ejercicio1.R
    ejercicio2.R
  lopez_maria/
    ejercicio1.R
    ejercicio2.R

tests/
  test_ejercicio1.R
  test_ejercicio2.R
```

A test file holds one or more functions named `test_<exercise>_<case>` that
return `TRUE` or `FALSE`.

```r
# tests/test_ejercicio1.R
test_ejercicio1_roots <- function() {
  all(quadratic_roots(1, 0, -1) == c(-1, 1))
}
test_ejercicio1_numeric <- function() {
  is.numeric(quadratic_roots(1, 0, -1))
}
```

## Running the grader

```r
library(corrector)

results <- grade_submissions("submissions/", test_dir = "tests/")
```

`results` is a `grade_results` object: a long-format data frame with one row
per test and the columns `student`, `exercise`, `test`, `status`, `message`
and `duration`. Status is one of `pass`, `fail`, `error`, `timeout`,
`missing`, or `source_error`. That tells a test that returned `FALSE` apart
from one that raised an error, ran out of time, or a file that was not
handed in or could not be loaded.

```r
head(as.data.frame(results, format = "long"))
```

For the wide view (one logical column per exercise) use
`as.data.frame(results, format = "wide")`. There `NA` means the exercise was
not handed in or the file could not be loaded.

While you write the tests, try them on a single file:

```r
grade_exercise("submissions/garcia_juan/ejercicio1.R", test_dir = "tests/")
```

## Trying it without real submissions

`example_results()` returns made-up results (8 students, 5 exercises) to try
the summaries, plots and exports. The package also ships test files for five
sample exercises: roots of a quadratic equation, word search, sorting,
simulation, and data frame transformation.

```r
grade_report(example_results())
list.files(system.file("examples", package = "corrector"))
```

## Summarising

`grade_report()` reduces the long results to per-exercise pass rates and
per-student scores, plus counts of errors, timeouts, and missing submissions.
A missing exercise counts as 0.

```r
grade_report(results)
```

`plot_report()` produces three plots: each student's score, the pass rate
per exercise, and a heatmap of the results. Pass `backend = "ggplot2"` to
use ggplot2, if installed. To save them to a PDF:

```r
pdf("report.pdf", width = 8, height = 5)
plot_report(results, ask = FALSE)
dev.off()
```

## Exporting

```r
export_to_csv(results, "grades.csv")               # wide by default
export_to_csv(results, "grades-long.csv", format = "long")
export_to_html(results, "report.html")
```

The HTML report colour-codes each cell by status and includes a per-student
breakdown of every test. To write to a Google Sheet (needs the googlesheets4
package):

```r
googlesheets4::gs4_auth()
export_to_sheets(results, "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/...")
```

## Partial credit, weights and feedback

`student_scores()` gives each exercise the fraction of its tests that pass,
with optional weights per test or per exercise, and a `total` grade where a
missing exercise counts as 0. `grade_report(scoring = "partial")` uses the
same rules. `grade_scale()` turns that score into a grade (1 to 10 with 60%
as a 4, by default). `export_feedback()` writes one Markdown file per
student, in Spanish or English depending on `lang`.

```r
grades <- student_scores(results, weights = c(ejercicio2 = 2))
grades$grade <- grade_scale(grades$total)
export_feedback(results, "feedback/", lang = "en")
```

## Similar submissions

`compare_submissions()` lists, for each exercise, the pairs of students with
very similar files, even after renaming variables or changing spacing or
comments. A high similarity does not prove copying; use it to pick what to
read by hand.

```r
compare_submissions("submissions/", min_similarity = 0.8)
```

## testthat, R Markdown and Quarto

Test functions can use testthat expectations (`library(testthat)` at the top
of the test file). Students can hand in `.R`, `.Rmd` or `.qmd` files, and file
names are matched ignoring case.

## Timeouts and untrusted code

The default engine, `"callr"`, runs each exercise in a fresh R subprocess
with a temporary working directory. Each test gets `timeout` seconds (default
10), and so does loading the student's file. If a test does not respond to
the limit (for example inside `Sys.sleep()`), the subprocess is killed once
the whole exercise passes `timeout` × number of tests + 5 seconds; tests that
already finished keep their result. Use `timeout = Inf` for no limit.

```r
results <- grade_submissions("submissions/", test_dir = "tests/", timeout = 30)
```

`engine = "inproc"` runs tests in the current R session. It is faster, but
`setTimeLimit()` does not interrupt every loop, and student code can change
your global environment.

For large classes, `workers` runs several subprocesses at the same time:

```r
results <- grade_submissions("submissions/", test_dir = "tests/", workers = 4)
```

corrector is not a sandbox. The `callr` engine protects your R session, not
your computer: student code can read and write any file your user can, use
the network, or run system commands. For code from people you do not trust,
run corrector inside a container or virtual machine without your credentials.
The `callr` and `inproc` engines block the common cheating tricks and report
the rest; `engine = "isolated"` keeps student code out of the process that
runs the tests. See `vignette("cheat-resistant-grading")`.

## Renaming students

The default student-name extractor takes the first underscore-separated
segment and applies title case (so `garcia_juan_12345` becomes `Garcia`).
Pass `student_name_fn` to override:

```r
results <- grade_submissions(
  "submissions/", test_dir = "tests/",
  student_name_fn = function(folder) {
    sub("_.*$", "", folder)
  }
)
```

## Moodle

`layout = "moodle"` reads the `.zip` from Moodle's "Download all
submissions", with or without "Download submissions in folders":

```r
results <- grade_submissions("assignment1.zip", test_dir = "tests/",
                             layout = "moodle")
```

To send the grades back, `export_moodle_feedback()` builds a `.zip` with one
feedback file inside each student's Moodle folder. On the assignment's
submissions page, use "Upload multiple feedback files in a zip"; the
assignment must have file feedback turned on.

```r
export_moodle_feedback(results, "feedback-assignment1.zip")
```
